title: I've always wanted to make a game that simulated choosing the right checkout lane. What mechanics should I add?
author: Synyster328

comments.author: Itchy-Individual3536
comments.body: Excuse me, dear, could I maybe jump in front of you? I only got these two items and my baby's waiting in the carpark!

comments.author: Itchy-Individual3536
comments.body: Make switching the lane more realistic by adding a delay (slower movement animation), during which other customers can get in line just before you (in the lane you were coming from and the lane you're heading at), making lane changes riskier (just like in real life). Similarly, open a new lane from time to time, where you can choose to change to, but others will change, too.

replies.author: Synyster328
replies.body: Nice, the risky lane switch is brilliant.

comments.author: story_of_the_beer
comments.body: You should add frustration sfx mechanics like 'C'mon... hurryup!' or someone just chatting at the register lol great idea otherwise

comments.author: Kopteeni
comments.body: I sometimes choose based on the profiles of the customers. It's a risky play queuing behind an elderly person even if the lane has fewer customers.
